headline: Rushil Decor files SEBI Reg 31(4) disclosure; substantial acquisition event triggered
sum: Rushil Decor Limited has filed a Regulation 31(4) disclosure under SEBI's Takeover Regulations, signalling a material acquisition event or crossing of the 5% shareholding threshold. The filing with NSE mandates public disclosure and triggers subsequent open offer and disclosure regimen under the Takeover Code.
implication: Regulation 31(4) filing is the mandatory gating disclosure; the acquirer identity, quantum and price remain embedded in the detailed schedule attached to the NSE filing - search the NSE archives directly for the full disclosure form to extract deal economics and conditions precedent.
detail: Under SEBI's Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers Regulations, 2011, any acquirer crossing 5% of voting rights (or 2% incremental threshold post-5%) must disclose within two trading days. This disclosure is the first public signal of a material shareholding event and is central to the open offer trigger mechanism. The article references a detailed schedule containing acquirer identity, acquisition quantum, price and conditions, but these specifics are not reproduced in the Bar & Bench summary.

framework.note: Mandatory disclosure within two trading days of crossing 5% threshold or entering acquirer agreement; forms the gating disclosure.
Defines 'Acquirer' and voting shares; central to determining disclosure trigger.
Open offer thresholds (25% / 26%) and exemptions from open offer requirements; downstream consequence of Reg 31(4) filing.
Comprehensive disclosure requirements for acquisitions of shares and voting rights; Reg 31(4) is a specific sub-rule for substantial acquisitions.
Corporate social responsibility implications may arise post-acquisition depending on acquirer group financials; not directly applicable but relevant for post-deal compliance.

framework.ref: Listed Entities (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, Regulation 4
framework.note: Acquirer and related parties subject to restricted period and trading restrictions once acquisition is announced or reasonably believed to be imminent.
SEBI derives rulemaking power for takeover regulation; provides the statutory foundation for Takeover Regulations.
